questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: The most exciting holidays in the world
Whether bucket lists are good for us
How to overcome a fear of flying
The history of the phrase 'kick the bucket'
questions.why: They discuss bucket lists, which can help people but have also been criticised.

questions.q: What criticism of bucket lists is mentioned at the start?
options: They are too expensive for most ordinary people
They make people lazy because they only dream
They take far too long to write and plan properly
They make people follow someone else's perfect life
questions.why: Sam says they've been accused of limiting imagination by encouraging people to follow someone else's idea.

questions.q: How does Neil feel about extreme activities?
options: He might try bungee-jumping if the rope was checked
He loves skydiving and does it every summer
He has already done all of them at least once
He would never try anything risky, even bungee-jumping
questions.why: He says 'Not really!' to skydiving, but bungee-jumping maybe, as long as someone checked the rope.

questions.q: Why did blogger Annette White make her bucket list?
options: To become famous online
To learn Spanish for work
To help her overcome anxiety
To raise money for charity
questions.why: She listed things as a way of improving her wellbeing, and Claudia Hammond says it was to overcome anxiety.

questions.q: According to Annette White, how has her bucket list helped her?
options: It has made her richer through her travel blog
Leaving her comfort zone made her fear smaller
It has helped her make lots of new friends abroad
It has helped her relax and enjoy life at home
questions.why: She says each step out of her comfort zone replaces fear with empowerment, so her 'fear bubble' got smaller.

questions.q: What is Linda Blair's opinion of bucket lists?
options: She is not really in favour of them
She thinks everyone should have one
She thinks they're only useful for older people
She has written one herself
questions.why: She says, “I'm not really in favour of bucket lists.”

questions.q: According to Linda Blair, how do people fool themselves with a bucket list?
options: They believe they will finish it quickly
They think it will make them happy forever
They copy other people's ideas
They feel they can somehow control death
questions.why: She says the list gives you the idea that you can somehow control when and what death will be.

questions.q: What does Linda Blair think a bucket list takes away?
options: Your free time
Your savings
The chance to be spontaneous
Your fear of the unknown
questions.why: She says, “A bucket list takes you away from the chance to be spontaneous.”
